newsitem.title: USA: PALFED says shareholder proposes co sale.
newsitem.headline: PALFED says shareholder proposes co sale.

text.p: PALFED Inc said on Wednesday a shareholder proposed it take immediate steps to achieve a sale, merger or other acquisition of PALFED.
The shareholder, Mid-Atlantic Investors, and its two partners, Jerry Zucker and Jerry Shearer, together owned 474,000 or 9.1 percent of the company's outstanding stock, PALFED said.
PALFED said its board unanimously opposed the proposal, and believed a forced sale was never in the company's best interests.

In a separate letter to John Troutman, PALFED's president and chief executive, Mid-Atlantic offered to withdraw its proposal if PALFED's board elected M. Jerry Garfinkle as a director, formed a merger and acquisitions committee with Garfinkle as a member, and engaged an investment adviser skilled in mergers, PALFED said.

But Troutman said: "We believe the company's current strategy of growth will build long-term shareholder value and the directors have no intention to abandon that strategy and sell the company solely to satisfy the demands of Mid-Atlantic and Messrs. Shearer and Zucker."
PALFED said it already had a strategic alternatives committee which considered mergers and acquisitions and also had engaged an investment advisor skilled in such matters.

The company also said Garfinkle did not have the corporate or community presence to represent it in Charleston and could not represent the interests of all shareholders, because he was as an attorney for Zucker.
